Video on surfaces, sound in the room#

A TV that plays in the lounge, a looping brand film on the lobby wall, a fountain you can hear before you see it. In 2.7 a scene's owner puts a video on any surface and sound anywhere in the room, and every visitor — in the viewer, in a private share, in an embed — gets playing screens that glow and audio that sits where its source is. WebGPU and WebGL2; streamed scenes (the .vpk your upload compiles to).

What you need#

  • A scene you own (signed in at /studio; upload or claim it).
  • A video: mp4 (H.264) or webm, up to 200 MB. Any size — the engine samples it at 512², so 720p is plenty; a 4K file only costs bandwidth.
  • Optional sound: mp3, m4a, ogg or wav, up to 20 MB per clip.

Files you upload are stored with the scene (ingest/<id>.media/<n>.mp4), served under its visibility (a private scene's video needs the share token, like its model) and deleted with it. You can also point at a file already on the same host; cross-origin URLs are refused (the frame is read back on the GPU and must not be tainted).

Put a video on a surface#

  1. Open the scene with ?author=1 (the Author bar appears; sign in first).
  2. Click Media in the scene chrome, then Pick a surface.
  3. Click the surface — the panel shows Material N — give it a video.
  4. Paste a same-origin URL or choose a file, then Add. The upload runs, the table saves, and the screen starts playing right away.
  5. Adjust Glow (0 = the frame as is; 1 is the default, up to 4). The screen is self-lit either way — it reads the same in a baked room as in a live-lit one. Tick Sound from this screen to play the video's own track from the surface.

The video covers the material's whole UV range the way its baked texture did: a screen modelled as one quad with 0–1 UVs shows the full frame; a material shared by several objects shows it on all of them. Up to four screens per scene.

Place an ambient sound#

  1. Media → Place ambient sound, then click where the sound lives (the fountain's basin, the speaker on the shelf).
  2. Paste a URL or choose a clip, Add.
  3. Set Radius — the distance at which it fades to silence (linear) — and Gain.

What visitors get#

  • Screens play muted and loop. A screen pauses when it is behind the visitor or farther than 40 m, and resumes the moment it is in view. Visitors with reduce motion set in their OS see one still frame.
  • A Sound chip appears in the scene chrome whenever the scene has audio. Browsers will not play sound until the visitor clicks something: the chip is that click, and the global mute. Each source is positioned (HRTF) and follows the camera as the visitor walks.
  • Everything is in the share link already — the table is stored with the scene and follows it through versions (a new upload keeps its screens).

From code#

Code
// Node / browser SDK — the same thing the Media panel does.
const clip = await verse.scenes.uploadMedia(id, mp4Bytes, "video/mp4");
await verse.scenes.setMedia(id, {
  media: [{ material: 3, url: `/${clip.path}`, emissive: 1.5, audio: true }],
  audio: [{ pos: [2, 1.2, -1], url: "/ingest/abc.media/2.mp3", radius: 6, gain: 0.8 }],
});

// Embed SDK — swap the table live (not saved), drive the mute.
viewer.setMedia({ media: [{ material: 3, url: "/ingest/abc.media/1.mp4" }], audio: [] });
viewer.on("media", (m) => console.log(m));
viewer.setAudioMuted(false); // after a click in your page

API: GET/PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/media, POST …/media/upload. Embed: setMedia / getMedia / setAudioMuted.

Limits, honestly#

  • Four screens per scene; frames are sampled at 512² and at most 30 fps, and a frame is dropped rather than queued when the previous one is still on its way to the GPU. Expect ~1–2 ms of render-worker time per playing screen per frame.
  • A screen is self-lit, not a light: it does not light the room, is not reflected by the environment probe, and the cinematic path tracer renders the material's own base colour.
  • Sound has no occlusion — a wall does not muffle it; use the radius.
  • Media must be same-origin. Classic GLB scenes (not streamed) have no media surfaces.
  • The owner's Media panel lives in the playground; embeds play the table and take setMedia from the host page but do not author.
